citation: "Wolf's Point and the Town of Chicago." Chicagology. Compiling A. T. Andreas, History of Chicago, and Fergus Historical Series.
note: Transcribes period and near-period accounts. Source for: the West Side as open prairie free from timber; the South Side timber belt running east to Wells and crossing Clark; the North Side 'thrifty heavy growth of timber'; the marshy river-shore strip of tall grass, reeds and rushes; the Public Square pond where Indians trapped muskrat and settlers hunted ducks; the slough draining that pond past the Tremont House site to the river at the foot of State Street; wild onions among the sedge grass. A finding aid — re-source images from the holding institution before use.
